statusText: Mapped policy state: BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES. Tail has crossed the block threshold to 26% and Stress is high at 70%.
recommendation: The overnight band break has extended into a second consecutive down-leg, with Nasdaq-100 futures holding within roughly 12 points of the session low while yields, volatility, crude and gold are aligned risk-negative and the US-Iran escalation remains unresolved. Repeated extension combined with session-extreme holding is the structure most hostile to mean reversion, so the mapped policy state moves to BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES. The conditional risk concentration remains the narrow 13:30-15:00 UTC window covering the US cash open and the simultaneous ISM Manufacturing and JOLTS releases. The assessment would ease back toward the WATCH band on an orderly retracement that reclaims and holds the 29,327 prior low, and would move toward the strong-block band only on further extension after failed retracements.
headline: Nasdaq-100 futures extend a second leg to 29,207 and hold near session lows as the global bond rout, $88 crude and a 4.79% US 10-year stay aligned
body: Nasdaq-100 futures have extended the overnight break into a second consecutive down-leg. At 09:15-09:17 UTC NQ traded 29,206.75-29,210.50, about -1.03% and roughly 306 points below the 29,513 previous close, on a session range of 29,195.75-29,571.25. Price sits only some 12 points above the session low, so the contract is holding at its extreme rather than repairing. That is a material change from the previous hour: at 08:30 UTC the index was at 29,351 with a 29,327 low, and it has since made a further low roughly 130 points below that without reclaiming the broken 29,434.75-29,570.00 overnight band. Two independent quote sources agree on the level and the range. The cross-asset stack is aligned in the same risk-negative direction. The US 10-year yield stands at 4.79%, its highest since January 2025, with the 2-year at 4.37%; Japan's 10-year government bond yield crossed 3% for the first time since September 1996, with the 5-year at a record 2.26% and the 2-year at a 31-year peak of 1.795%; the German 10-year is near 3.34%, the highest since 2011. Reuters reporting attributes the synchronised selloff to oil-driven inflation pressure, expected central-bank tightening, record sovereign and AI-related corporate issuance and deteriorating fiscal conditions. WTI is $87.84 (+2.43%) and Brent $92.24 (+1.93%) after the US-Iran exchange around Larak Island and Iranian strikes on bases in Jordan, with stated US threats extended toward Kharg Island, Iran's principal oil export hub. VIX is 15.84, up 6.16%, at its session high of 15.86, and gold is down 1.25%, so the move reads as broad de-risking rather than a rotation. Market pricing for a 25 basis-point September hike remains near 60-65% after Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's Jackson Hole address. The distinguishing feature against the previous hour is that a single directional leg has now become repeated extension with the index pinned near its session low, which is the specific structure that denies mean reversion. Combined with aligned yields, volatility, energy and gold, an aligned catalyst stack later today and an unresolved geopolitical escalation vector, that clears the threshold for an elevated reading. Tail is therefore raised from 22% to 26%, the low end of the elevated band, mapping to BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES. It is not set higher because the absolute move remains about 1%, VIX is still low in absolute terms at under 16, price discovery has been orderly rather than discontinuous, and the intra-hour path is known through level and range rather than tick structure. Stress is raised to 70% for the deepening bond rout and the energy stack. Confidence is 85% on cross-verified futures levels, yields, crude, volatility, a verified event calendar and verified current reporting, moderated because tick-level retracement detail is not available. Delayed shared cross-asset context collected at 05:50 UTC is more than three hours old, well beyond the 90-minute freshness bound, and predates both down-legs, so it has not been used as evidence for the current price path.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding clock-hours carry a published Claude assessment. Twenty-three of them mapped to the EA_ON band with Tail between 9 and 17 and Stress climbing from 47 to 58, and dominant mode was mixed in 22 of the 24. The single earlier Tail peak of 17 came in the 09:00 UTC hour on August 31 during a European event/whipsaw window. Through the August 31 US session Stress rose steadily as crude extended on the Larak Island exchange, the 10-year pushed to its highest level since January 2025 and September rate-hike odds firmed after the Jackson Hole address, while Tail stayed compressed between 9 and 13 because the price path itself remained two-sided. The overnight hours held that pattern with Stress at 50-58 and Tail at 9-11. Only the final lookback hour, 08:00 UTC on September 1, broke the pattern, with Tail at 22 and mode trend-down as the overnight band gave way. The current hour continues that break rather than reversing it.
outlookSummary: The base case over the next 24 hours is that today's rates-led repricing resolves into two-sided trade rather than into a persistent no-retracement path, but the projection now starts from an observed second down-leg rather than from a contained range, so Tail stays inside the block band through the European morning and the first US hours. Conditional risk concentrates in the 13:30-15:00 UTC danger window covering the US cash open, the final S&P Global Manufacturing PMI and the simultaneous ISM Manufacturing and JOLTS releases, where forecast Tail peaks at 29 and Stress at 76 with mode projected event/whipsaw, still below the strong-block threshold. The path is then projected to return to the WATCH band from 16:00 UTC as post-release volatility decays, with a flow-driven uptick in the 19:00 UTC power hour and an after-hours dispersion checkpoint as Palo Alto Networks, Dell Technologies and MongoDB report. Tail is projected back inside the EA_ON band from 22:00 UTC, reaching its low around 03:00-05:00 UTC before firming modestly with the Tokyo JGB reopen and again into the September 2 European session ahead of ADP. The projection would be invalidated by observed further extension after failed retracements, NQ pinning to session lows through the US afternoon, another leg in the global bond rout, or a fresh geopolitical discontinuity affecting Gulf energy flows.
